newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO show of force at Karadzic house.
newsitem.headline: NATO show of force at Karadzic house.

text.p: NATO troops staged a show of force with armoured personnel carriers and helicopters around the home of leading war crimes suspect and former Bosnian Serb president Radovan Karadzic on Saturday.
Eyewitnesses said French and Italian units were involved in the action near Karadzic's home on the outskirts of the nationalist stronghold of Pale.
The forces withdrew after an hour and it was not known whether Karadzic, who is protected by a strong force of bodyguards, was in the house at the time.

Karadzic and his former army commander General Ratko Mladic are wanted for trial by the U.N. war crimes tribunal in the Netherlands for atrocities committed by the Bosnian Serbs during the 1992-95 war.
Although Western countries have frequently demanded his surrender, no attempt has been made so far to arrest him by NATO, partly because of the risk of casualties.
The policy adopted by the peacekeepers has been to arrest war crimes suspects if their are encountered but not to hunt them down.
But earlier this month British NATO troops killed a Serb suspect who resisted arrest in the northwestern town of Prijedor and arrested another who is now in custody in The Hague where the court sits.
The raid angered Bosnian Serb leaders and has been followed by a series of minor bomb attacks on international targets in Serb territory which NATO said was an attempt at low level intimidation.
